candidates.classification: Source-derived authoring/runtime admission disagreement, extending the same previously documented 059 numeric boundary.
candidates.trace: quest_catalog_validation checks authored monster combat weight as a finite positive f64 no greater than f32::MAX, while MonsterCombat stores f32. A hypothetical weight 1e-100 is positive as f64 but rounds to zero in IEEE-754 binary32. The pinned non-arbitrary-precision serde_json Value deserializer dispatches an f64 to the serde_core f32 visitor, which casts without rejecting zero. The build script validates raw JSON values and emits the original values, whereas lazy catalog initialization validates the raw documents, deserializes them to typed CatalogDocument values and has Catalog::compile reject a monster whose typed weight is <= 0. If that decoder path is used, the catalog expect then panics on first initialization. This is source and arithmetic reasoning, not an executed edit, product parser, build or runtime failure.
candidates.corpus_and_consumers: Read-only inspection of every pinned content/quests YAML file finds 25 authored monsters, all in bestiary.yaml; the minimum is skeleton at 18.0 kg. A hypothetical author could substitute a tiny positive skeleton weight, conditional on all other validation and decoding gates. The selected quest-generation description and local-problem source paths call the lazy catalogue, but no call, generated world, active enemy or deployment incident was observed.
candidates.safeguards_and_limits: The runtime compilation guard rejects zero before publishing the typed catalogue, so this is a fail-closed initialization disagreement rather than an accepted zero-mass combatant. The actual feature graph and runtime JSON decoder behavior were not resolved; the non-arbitrary-precision branch is explicitly conditional. Source inspection does not establish every build-time content checker, downstream consumer, other fields, product configuration or support for deliberately microscopic threats.
candidates.connected_repair: If positive finite f32 weight is the intended authoring contract, validate positivity and finiteness after conversion at the quest authoring boundary, preserving representable positive values and the runtime defence. Share a numeric helper with other catalogues only where units, bounds, ownership and error behavior agree; reconcile the related equipment-dimension entry and earlier PL13-186 scope before choosing a common remedy.
candidates.later_acceptance: After separate implementation and product-validation authorization, cover zero, negative, nonfinite, positive underflow, smallest representable positive values, ordinary authored weights and f32 maximum boundaries through actual build admission and lazy catalogue initialization under supported feature sets.
